It's very nice and refreshing to see UNIX being utilized in other places. The gameplay may be repetitive, but it is nonetheless challenging and quite fun. The learning curve is good, especially with the ability to look back on notes at any time.  The storyline as well as the missions kept me invested. It is a fun although not 100% true reflection of what it feels like to navigate through the terminal.

So you're looking for a game about hacking, eh? Well let me tell you this is about as perfect as you'll get!

In this game you start out on a quest searching for a lost hacker named "Bit". Your journey will lead you through many various situations varying in difficulty all while using the same simple command lines making the game fun and easy to learn but when needed to go fast it can become difficult managing your tasks.


UI I feel is splendid. The netmap is simple and easy to use throughout the entire game with the only downside being it gets cluttered towards the end. The command box and log is where you spend most of your time and the way it is formatted is perfect. 

Storyline is a bit hard to follow but it stays on one main goal, helping Bit and finding him. You'll join various factions and help them but it all ties together in an ending worth achieving.

The soundtrack while somewhat mundane at times changes depending on the situation to be faster and more energetic but it can be somewhat repetitive.

I give this game a 4/5 for it being simple yet remaining fun the entire time. The storyline held me in and had me actively wanting to progress to find out more, and the soundtrack added to the intensity and energy making it an amazing experience. Even when you finish the main story the steam workshop has many amazing addons and there's even s special secret after you beat the game ;)

Great game.

Its pretty well thought out and does a good job of making a 'game' out of some basic security concepts.  There are times where your real familiarity with unix will frustrate at times but over all the "network" that is created and the nodes (computers) connected to it is a convincing enough atmosphere to keep you engaged.

There are some minor play issues that a quick google search will resolve (where you have the right answer but you are missing a fine detail in your execution).  Largely I think the game resolves to more of a puzzle type game where you need to piece together clues and the truly curious (hack-minded) are rewarded depending on how far down the bunny hole you really want to dig into.  I found cases where there were things I could dig into that were orthogonal to the story line and the end-credits clarified that there are some in deep details that can be explored.  To me this shows a really well-thought out world and the author should be commended for that depth that might not be immediately obvious.

My only criticism is there is occasionally some juvenile writing that given the implied seriousness of the plot seems a little out of place.  However, I would say the bang-for-your-buck with this game is FAR better than a lot of supposed AAA titles that entertained much less and cost far more.

it never crashed once either.. and that deserves an award as well.

I usually don't write reviews but this game is just so incredible that i just had to. I had this game laying around in my steam library when i decided to do some steam cleaning (This is when i download a game, test it out, if i like, I keep it, If I don't, I remove the game from my account) I got up to Hacknet, and tried it out. I never expected to play the entire game and finish it. the Story was phenomenal (sometimes confusing though) and got attached right off the bat. If you want a game where you can code and have to progress through a story at the same time, I recommend this game. The soundtrack is catchy and won't get annoying after a while. The commands are easy to learn, and you'll often find yourself feeling like a hacking master. The ending is rewarding and worth it. There is quite a bit of secrets and hidden aspects of the game as well so you'll be wanting to play again to find them. You'll probably get a couple hours out of this game, even more if you plan on completing it 100%. The developer did a amazing job making the game really fun and interesting throughout the entire story.

If you're picking out games to purchase, make Hacknet one of them.

Hacknet is probably one of my favorite storyline games I've played. First off... I just love the execution of the game. All of the typing and command lines and all made me feel super badass. As for playability, there's a quick learning curve for people who have no knowledge of programming. If you're a computer tech student like I was, you'll feel right at home.

The storyline is interesting and there's little irc logs that have some funny conversations in them.

The thing I loved the most though was the surprising moral dilemmas you face!!!! Especially in the dlc. 

Basically if you love storylines, feeling like a cool hacker, and good music.... this is an amazing game that you'll love!! Plus ... WORKSHOP!

This isn't a whole lot more complicated than the description describes.

But it is quite a bit of fun.

I was a bit scared about this kind of games, but I've played a lot in my past of those things... well, hacknet is a good surprise on many aspects.

First of all there are tons of good music that take you deep into the dark code. They are not so good as other hack games that I've played but they are many and the quality is average good. So the result is positive.

About the code you slowly advance from zero to conquering many executables that opens doors previously closed. In my opition there could be some aspect as the power of the tool or the power of the computer that should be enanched with points or something. So the focus has been clearly put elsewhere, and this location is in the plot.

I means that the interesting part of the game is not only the break of a system with temporized use of tools, but moreover the text and the histories that lies inside the computers that you open. 

Easter egg are everywhere, from zeroCool to Encom, to Monogame DLL, to the medical hack that I've already seen elsewhere.. And the immersion is strong because some hacking trascent from the game itself, scaring a bit. The Open Cd is still there, as an old game that I don't really remember now.. funny!

I've also found an unexpected extra level... the game damaged entirely my savegame, showing error in the main page.. the real savegame. Fortunately exploring the properties of this XML in my windows there was the possibility to restore a backup of 2 mission before the point I reached. This is confusing, of cours it's not a part of the game, but If I wasn't playing this game I would never discovered a Windows checkpoint of the user files... you must be curious, always. 

Well, risking the game quit for savegame damage, but reaching the end anyway, I found that the entire production was funny and entertaining. 
The extra level was good and someway hardcode (Labyrinths), but my last mission failed because I was still reading what should I have to do when the time runs out.

Good works with this Monogame piece.  I'm a coder and the final level used a music that I used too in a coding game of mine.. that was too much for me. Something strange lies behind all of these coincidences!

Time to hail
